title: Why inertia is not a force
canonical_question: Why is inertia not itself a force?
summary: Inertia is the tendency of a body to keep its state of motion, but it does not push or pull anything.
When a bus stops and you feel thrown forward, no "inertia force" pushed you; you simply kept moving while the bus slowed.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: A property, not a push
sections.body_md: Inertia is the tendency of a body to keep its state of motion, but it does not push or pull anything. A force is an interaction between bodies; inertia is just how strongly one body resists change. Calling inertia a force confuses a property with an action.

sections.heading: The lurch is not a force
sections.body_md: When a bus stops and you feel thrown forward, no "inertia force" pushed you; you simply kept moving while the bus slowed. The feeling is continued motion, not a new push. Naming it a force invents something that is not there.

key_points: Inertia is a property, not a force.
The forward lurch is continued motion.
core.bridge_to_parent: It deepens the inertia concept rather than applying it.
